parameters.content:
## 1 · Age the book

Runs every morning, or on demand. Customers, open invoices and the collection log are each read once.

The collection log is the part that matters: it is the memory this workflow keeps of who was already contacted and when. Without it, a scheduled chaser mails the same customer every single day until they pay, which is how automated collections destroys a relationship a human would have fixed with one phone call.

## 2 · Every reason NOT to chase, first

The order is deliberate. Settled, in dispute, or covered by a promise that has not expired — none of those get chased, whatever the age. A broken promise moves the account one rung HARDER, because the trust was already spent.

Only then does the ladder apply: due soon and large enough for a courtesy note, 1-7 days a reminder, 8-21 firm, 22-45 final, 46+ collections.

Then the grouping, which is the point of the whole piece: one message per CUSTOMER, listing every one of their overdue invoices, pitched at the hardest stage any single one has reached. Twelve overdue invoices become four emails, not twelve.

## 3 · Three outcomes

A reminder that assumes the customer may simply have missed it. A final notice that states the credit consequence plainly and names the person to call. Or a written record of why we deliberately said nothing today — restraint that is not recorded is indistinguishable from a broken workflow.

The cadence guard sits in front of all of it: a customer contacted yesterday is not contacted again today, even if a new invoice has just tipped over.

## 4 · Record, then report

Every decision, chased or held, is written back keyed on customer plus date. Running twice in one morning updates that row rather than making tomorrow think the customer was chased twice.

The morning report leads with the aging and a probability-weighted cash forecast, because that is the number a finance lead actually needs: not how many emails went out, but how much of this is really coming in.

## 5 · Where it goes

All four are switched off and carry no credential, wired as side branches so the log write and the report are unaffected by whether they are on.

Gmail for the customer-facing messages, Slack for the account manager whose relationship is about to get difficult. Turn one on by attaching a credential and picking the channel or address.
